new_results.statement: For Y=X S(V)+R(V), with X an original independent cap-one coordinate, arbitrary correlation between S and R, bank submeasure mass m, and slope-pushforward density cap L, H=L/m, one has nu_Y{|Y-t|<=rho} <= m F(4Hrho), F(q)=q(1+log(1/q)) for q<=1 and 1 for q>=1; hence the translated logarithmic potential is <=m Omega_0(4HA).

After an outer invertible indefinite original-coordinate pair B with D=|det B| and kappa=sigma_min(B), a slope component of mass m and cap L contributes density at most 8 sqrt(mL/kappa)+2m/sqrt(D). For a positive decomposition the exact summation cost is 8 kappa^(-1/2) sum sqrt(m_j L_j)+2D^(-1/2)sum m_j; caps L_j<=H m_j preserve the whole-law constant.

For zero-self hub remainder X0[s0+2d(aX3+bX4-beta)]+R with |b|>=|a|, arbitrary same-bank R, and outer pair (D,kappa), arbitrary countable fragmentation of X3 while X4 remains whole preserves ||p_Q||inf <=4sqrt(2)/sqrt(|db|kappa)+2/sqrt(D).

For target-valid Q=2U1U2+2X0(X3+X4) with remote N-fragment cap-one laws, the whole and one-sided-fragment compiler gives <=4sqrt(2)+2, whereas independently fragmenting both shear variables and summing the same cellwise certificate gives 4sqrt(2N)+2. This is not a density lower bound or QFORM counterexample.

partner_result_applied.use: Applied its one-sided subprobability shear density cap m/|b| to the random hub slope, yielding a fragmentwise density estimate linear in the unnormalized fragment mass.

first_unpaid_implication: QFORM-ZERO-HUB-SLOPE-OR-WHOLE-VOLUME-EXIT-v1: before active fragmentation in every surviving no-pivot/N3 state, expose either a useful outer pair plus exact zero-self original-coordinate hub with mass-homogeneous whole-bank slope cap, or a whole-law D'/D5/ridge/mixed-hub/bank exit; small nonzero hub self-curvature cannot be discarded perturbatively.
